topic: Template Function with Type Parameters and Chrono Duration
explanation: This concept demonstrates how C++ templates enable generic programming by allowing functions to operate with different data types. Specifically, the 'try_lock_for' function is a template member function that accepts a duration parameter with arbitrary representation and period, leveraging the 'chrono' library's flexible duration types. Templates provide compile-time polymorphism, enabling code reuse and type safety across various clock and duration types in concurrent programming scenarios.
syntax:
template <class Clock, class Duration>
bool try_lock_for(const std::chrono::duration<Clock, Duration>& rel_time);
example_explanation: This example defines a class 'TimerMutex' with a template member function 'try_lock_for' that accepts any 'std::chrono::duration' type, parameterized by Clock and Duration. In 'main', the function is called with different duration types (seconds, milliseconds, nanoseconds), demonstrating how templates enable the function to work seamlessly with various time representations. This showcases C++'s powerful template system for generic, type-safe, and flexible code in concurrent programming contexts.
